findings: Pinned TensorFlow entry point constructs twelve sparse neural models in three groups, using classes named RegressionHuber and RegressionClf; static method-dispatch review below identifies an effective-loss mismatch.
README records a twelve-component affine blend with an intercept. The intake FM-FTRL/CNN/Ridge blend is not established by this source.
The short golf demonstration is distinct from the full winning implementation and must not replace it.

tensorflow_dispatch.conclusion: The Huber-named TensorFlow subclass does not override the builder called by fit. A port must not silently replace this with Huber loss while claiming parity.
tensorflow_dispatch.checks: AST confirms caller method name, missing subclass override and inherited mean_squared_error call; no historical TensorFlow runtime was executed.

model_scope_followup.mxnet_scope: Entry point declares twelve models, but a source comment identifies four more same models in the best submission. Exact extra-model seeds and winner artifact identity remain unqualified.
model_scope_followup.blend: Shared merge helper fits positive-coefficient Lasso with alpha0.0001, random selection, random_state9999, max_iter1000 and an intercept in log1p response space, then applies expm1. README coefficients are reported fitted values, not an interchangeable plain probability average.
branch_differences: TensorFlow and MXNet use different hidden widths, regularization and learning-rate decay; they are not interchangeable backends without parity evidence.
